docs.title: FontLab Instamix
docs.text:
Instamix is the installer that FontLab 9 scripts, Python packages and plugins use to reach a user's FontLab. It is a stdlib-only Python package, so it runs inside FontLab's embedded Python 3.11 as well as from a terminal, and it records every file it places, so an uninstall removes exactly what it installed.

This site is a guide for FontLab developers. It follows one piece of work from the first line of code to a user's Scripts menu:

  1. Develop a script or a Python package against a live FontLab, with edits that take effect without reinstalling.
  2. Write a plugin: a reporter, filter, tool, palette or general extension that FontLab loads at launch.
  3. Package the work as a .fontlabext extension or as a project with a [tool.fontlab-install] table.
  4. Deploy it into a FontLab data folder from the command line, from FontLab's Python panel or with install.vfpy.
  5. Deliver it to users as a zip, a Git repository or a PyPI release, and ship updates.

The reference lists every command, manifest key and project key.

docs.title: Install Instamix
docs.text: Download install.vfpy and open it with File > Open in FontLab 9. It bootstraps Instamix without another Python package installer. The script is distributed under the project licence.

docs.title: Two routes
docs.text:
Route You ship Best for Extension a .fontlabext folder or a .fontlabextz zip with a manifest.fontlabextj scripts, encodings, codepages, actions and data files; no Python packaging Project a repository with pyproject.toml, a [tool.fontlab-install] table and an install.vfpy stub Python packages, scripts and plugin bundles, with dependencies on PyPI or on other FontLab projects

Both routes end in the same place. Instamix writes an extension record under <data>/Extensions/Library/, places the files in FontLab's folders and adds an uninstaller to the Scripts menu.

docs.title: Try it in two minutes
docs.text:
Every command takes --data-dir, so you can try instamix on a scratch folder without touching your FontLab:

git clone https://github.com/fontlabcom/fontlab-python-instamix
cd fontlab-python-instamix
uvx fontlab-python-instamix --data-dir /tmp/fl ext install examples/com.example.hello.fontlabext
uvx fontlab-python-instamix --data-dir /tmp/fl ext list
uvx fontlab-python-instamix --data-dir /tmp/fl ext uninstall com.example.hello

The first command prints installed com.example.hello 1.0.0 (4 paths). The extension's script lands in /tmp/fl/Scripts/com.example.hello/ and its encoding in /tmp/fl/Encoding/com.example.hello/.

docs.title: Deliver
docs.text: Delivery is how a user gets your package. Choose the channel by who your users are.

docs.title: A zip for anyone
docs.text:
Send a .fontlabextz file. A user with instamix installs it from the Python panel:

import fontlab_instamix as im
im.install("/path/to/com.example.countglyphs.fontlabextz")

or from a terminal with uvx fontlab-python-instamix ext install com.example.countglyphs.fontlabextz. Attach the zip to a GitHub release so each version has a stable download.

docs.title: A Git repository
docs.text:
Commit pyproject.toml with its [tool.fontlab-install] table and the install.vfpy stub. Users download or clone the repository and open install.vfpy in FontLab. The stub fetches instamix from PyPI when it is missing, so the user needs nothing else.

Developers who clone the repository get links instead of copies, so a pull and a FontLab restart bring in the new code.

docs.title: PyPI
docs.text:
Publish the project as a normal Python distribution when other packages depend on it. Other projects then list it in dependencies, and instamix installs it with uv into FontLab's site-packages. Users can also install it directly:

uvx fontlab-python-instamix pkg install fontlab-my-tools

pkg install places only the Python distribution. Scripts and plugins are installed by bootstrap from a checkout or by the project's install.vfpy.

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text:
1. Bump the version: tag the commit with hatch-vcs, or edit [project].version or the manifest version.
  2. Install into a scratch folder with --data-dir and check the printed path count.
  3. Install into your own FontLab, restart and run each script and plugin.
  4. Uninstall and check that nothing is left behind except files you changed.
  5. Build the deliverable: wrap … --zip, or uv build for PyPI.
  6. Publish the zip on a GitHub release or the distribution on PyPI, and update the install.vfpy stub if instamix changed.

docs.title: Supporting users
docs.text: Ask users for the output of fontlab-instamix env and the list from Scripts > Instamix > List Extensions. The install log in <data>/Extensions/.instamix/install.log records each install and uninstall with its time and version.

docs.title: Deploy
docs.text: Deploying means placing a package in a FontLab data folder. Instamix does the same work from three places: a terminal, FontLab's Python panel and an install.vfpy that FontLab opens.

docs.title: The data folder
docs.text:
Instamix finds <data> in this order:

  1. --data-dir on the command line
  2. $FONTLAB_DATA_DIR
  3. fontlab.flPreferences().dataPathDefault, inside FontLab
  4. ~/Library/Application Support/FontLab/FontLab 9 on macOS, Documents\FontLab\FontLab 9 on Windows

fontlab-instamix env prints the folder it chose, together with the Python version, platform and site-packages path.

docs.title: From a terminal
docs.text:
fontlab-instamix ext install dist/com.example.countglyphs.fontlabextz
fontlab-instamix ext install examples/com.example.hello.fontlabext --copy
fontlab-instamix bootstrap path/to/project
fontlab-instamix pkg install fonttools

ext install stores a copy of the extension in Extensions/Library/ and links each file from that copy into place, so the source folder can be deleted afterwards. --copy copies the files instead of linking; Windows always copies. bootstrap links straight to the files in your checkout, so edits there take effect after a FontLab restart. bootstrap installs a project from its [tool.fontlab-install] table and prints, for example, installed com.example.mytools (13 paths).

Restart FontLab after an install. FontLab reads Scripts, plugins and site-packages at launch.

docs.title: From FontLab's Python panel
docs.text:
import fontlab_instamix as im
im.install("/path/to/com.example.countglyphs.fontlabextz")
im.install_project("/path/to/project")
im.installed()
im.uninstall("com.example.countglyphs")

Instamix must already be in FontLab's site-packages. Open install.vfpy from the instamix repository once, or let a project stub fetch it.

docs.title: With install.vfpy
docs.text: Open a project's install.vfpy in FontLab with File > Open. The stub installs instamix if needed, installs the project and shows a message. This is the route for users who do not use a terminal.

docs.title: What gets written
docs.text:
For each install instamix writes:

  • the package files in FontLab's folders: Scripts, Encoding, Codepage, Actions, Data, Extensions/<kind>/ and python/3.11/site-packages
  • Extensions/Library/<id>.fontlabext, holding the manifest
  • Extensions/.instamix/<id>.json, a ledger of every placed path, and a line in Extensions/.instamix/install.log
  • Scripts/Instamix/List Extensions.py and Scripts/Instamix/Uninstall <id>.py, so users can manage installs from the Scripts menu
  • for a project, a <name>-<version>.dist-info folder whose INSTALLER reads fontlab-instamix

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
fontlab-instamix ext uninstall com.example.mytools

Instamix removes the paths in the ledger. A file the user changed after the install stays in place and is reported. PyPI dependencies stay installed, because other packages may need them; remove them with pkg uninstall.

docs.title: Update
docs.text: Install the new version over the old one. Instamix removes the files the old version placed, then places the new ones. If anything fails, it rolls back to the previous version.

docs.title: Develop
docs.text:
FontLab 9 runs Python 3.11 inside the application. Your code reaches it through FontLab's data folder, which instamix calls <data>:

Folder What FontLab does with it <data>/Scripts/ lists every .py and .vfpy file in the Scripts menu, by subfolder <data>/python/3.11/site-packages/ adds it to sys.path, so import mytools works in scripts, plugins and the Python panel <data>/Extensions/<kind>/ holds plugin bundles that fontlabapp.plugins loads at launch (see Plugins) <data>/Encoding/, <data>/Codepage/, <data>/Actions/, <data>/Data/ encodings, codepages, actions and data files

Run fontlab-instamix env to see the folder on your machine. Inside FontLab it reports "in_fontlab": true.

docs.title: Lay out a project
docs.text:
Keep scripts and the code they share in one repository:

my-fontlab-tools/
  pyproject.toml
  install.vfpy              # instamix stub, written by `fontlab-instamix stub .`
  src/mytools/__init__.py   # importable package: shared code
  Scripts/MyTools/SayHello.py
  Extensions/reporters/NodeCount.fontlabReporter/   # optional plugin bundle

A script is a plain Python file. Start it with an #FLM: comment that names it, keep the logic in your package, and keep the script short:

#FLM: Say Hello
import fontlab
from mytools import hello

package = fontlab.flWorkspace.instance().currentPackage
print(hello(), len(package.glyphs()) if package else "no font open")

docs.title: Install from the checkout
docs.text:
Add a [tool.fontlab-install] table to pyproject.toml (see Package) and install the checkout once:

uvx fontlab-python-instamix bootstrap .

Instamix links each file instead of copying it, so the installed script and package are your working files:

  • Scripts read your current source every time you run them from the menu.
  • Package code is cached once imported. Restart FontLab after you change it.
  • Plugin bundles load at launch. Restart FontLab after you change them.

On Windows, or where a symlink fails, instamix copies. Run bootstrap again after each edit there. Use --copy to force copies on any system, for example to test what a user gets.

docs.title: Python dependencies
docs.text:
FontLab's Python has no pip. Do not run pip from sys.executable: inside FontLab that is the application, not a Python interpreter. Declare dependencies in [project].dependencies and let bootstrap install them, or install them by hand:

fontlab-instamix pkg install fonttools "git+https://github.com/owner/repo"
fontlab-instamix pkg list

Instamix fetches its own uv into <data>/python/uv when none is on PATH (fontlab-instamix uv fetch) and installs into <data>/python/3.11/site-packages for Python 3.11 on your platform. Environment markers in dependency strings are evaluated for Python 3.11 and the host system, not for the Python that runs instamix.

For an editor or a type checker, fontlab-instamix venv creates or verifies <data>/.venv for Python 3.11. New environments use a managed .pth to read the canonical package directory. An existing compatible environment with site-packages linked directly to that exact directory is reused without changing its files. Other escaping paths, mismatched runtimes and unrelated managed-path files are refused.

docs.title: Test without FontLab
docs.text:
Point every command at a scratch folder to see exactly which files an install places:

uvx fontlab-python-instamix --data-dir /tmp/fl bootstrap .
find /tmp/fl -type f

This proves the layout, not the behaviour. Run scripts and plugins in FontLab 9 before you release them: an offline check cannot show menus, drawing, Undo or the state of an open font.

docs.title: Package
docs.text: Instamix accepts two kinds of package. Pick the extension format for plain files and the project format for anything that ships a Python package or depends on one.

docs.title: Extension: .fontlabext
docs.text:
An extension is a folder named with a reverse-DNS id, such as com.example.hello.fontlabext. It holds a manifest.fontlabextj at its root and the files the manifest names:

com.example.hello.fontlabext/
├── manifest.fontlabextj
├── scripts/
│   └── Hello.py
└── encoding/
    └── hello.enc

{"id": "com.example.hello", "name": "Hello", "version": "1.0.0",
 "min_fontlab": "9.0",
 "install": [{"from": "scripts", "to": "Scripts/{}"},
             {"from": "encoding/*.enc", "to": "Encoding/{}"}]}

Each install entry copies or links the files under from into to. A destination starts with a target: Scripts, Actions, Codepage, Data, Encoding or site-packages, in any case. . is the target root, {} is the extension name without .fontlabext, and {var} is a value from the manifest's vars. Unknown variables, unknown targets, .. and unknown manifest keys (other than this_file) are errors, so a typo fails the install instead of placing files in the wrong folder.

A manifest can also name Python packages and requirements:

"python": {"requires": ["fonttools>=4"], "packages": ["src/hello"]}

docs.title: Wrap a single script
docs.text:
You do not need to write the manifest by hand for a script:

fontlab-instamix wrap CountGlyphs.py --id com.example.countglyphs \
    --name "Count Glyphs" --version 1.0.0 --out dist --zip

This writes dist/com.example.countglyphs.fontlabext with the script under scripts/ and a manifest that installs it into Scripts/com.example.countglyphs/. --zip also writes dist/com.example.countglyphs.fontlabextz. wrap accepts .py and .vfpy files, or a folder of them.

docs.title: Zip: .fontlabextz
docs.text: A .fontlabextz is a zip that holds one or more .fontlabext folders. Use it to send extensions as one file. Instamix refuses members with absolute paths, drive letters or ... An install.vfpy hook inside a zip runs only when the user passes --run-hooks.

docs.title: Project: [tool.fontlab-install]
docs.text:
A project is an ordinary Python repository. Add a table to pyproject.toml:

[project]
name = "fontlab-my-tools"
version = "0.2.0"

[tool.fontlab-install]
id = "com.example.mytools"
name = "fontlab-my-tools"
packages = ["src/mytools"]
scripts = "Scripts"
extensions = "Extensions"
dependencies = ["fonttools>=4.50"]
  • id is required and must be reverse-DNS. It names the extension record and the uninstaller.
  • name should be the distribution name from [project].name. Instamix uses it for the <name>-<version>.dist-info folder it writes into site-packages.
  • packages lists package folders to place in <data>/python/3.11/site-packages.
  • scripts is a folder whose subfolders become FontLab Scripts menu folders. Scripts/MyTools/SayHello.py installs as Scripts/MyTools/SayHello.py.
  • extensions is a folder of plugin bundles (<kind>/<Name>.fontlab<Kind>).
  • dependencies are PEP 508 requirements. Instamix installs them with uv, evaluating markers for Python 3.11 on the host system. A dependency on another FontLab project that is checked out beside yours is installed from that checkout.

Instamix skips __pycache__, *.pyc, *.vfpyc and .DS_Store. It reads the version from [project].version, a hatch-vcs version file, PKG-INFO or git describe, in that order.

docs.title: The install.vfpy stub
docs.text:
Users install a project by opening install.vfpy in FontLab. Write the stub with:

fontlab-instamix stub .

The stub imports an installed instamix 1.0.13 or later. If there is none, or the installed one is older, it uses a sibling fontlab-python-instamix checkout, or downloads the instamix wheel from PyPI and checks its SHA-256. If that fails, the older copy is put back. Then it installs the project and shows a message with the id and version. Commit the stub; rerun stub --force to update it.

docs.title: Which to choose
docs.text: Need Format One script or a few wrap → .fontlabextz Encodings, codepages, actions, data files extension with a manifest A Python package for other scripts to import project Plugins (reporters, filters, tools, palettes) project with extensions Dependencies from PyPI or other FontLab projects project

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
A plugin is a folder bundle that FontLab loads at launch through the fontlabapp.plugins framework of fontlab-fontlabapp. The bundle's name ends in its kind, and it lives in the matching <data>/Extensions/ subfolder:

Kind Folder Bundle suffix Base class reporter reporters .fontlabReporter Reporter filter filters .fontlabFilter Filter tool tools .fontlabTool Tool palette palettes .fontlabPalette Palette general general .fontlabGeneral General

fontlab-python-plugmix holds working examples of each kind.

docs.title: A reporter bundle
docs.text:
Extensions/reporters/NodeCount.fontlabReporter/
  plugin.json
  node_count.py

plugin.json declares the plugin:

{
  "id": "node_count",
  "name": "Node Count",
  "kind": "reporter",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "entry": "node_count:NodeCount",
  "min_app_version": "1.2.10"
}
  • id, name and kind must match the class's name, title and kind. Ids are unique across all kinds.
  • version has three parts.
  • entry is module:Class; the module sits inside the bundle. The bundle needs no __init__.py.
  • min_app_version is the lowest fontlab-fontlabapp version the plugin needs.

The class receives an immutable snapshot of the glyph and returns marks to draw:

from fly.ap.plugins.reporter import Mark, Reporter
from fly.ap.plugins.snapshot import GlyphSnapshot


class NodeCount(Reporter):
    """Write the node count of each contour at its first node."""

    name = "node_count"
    title = "Node Count"

    def compute(self, snapshot: GlyphSnapshot) -> list[Mark]:
        marks = []
        for contour in snapshot.contours:
            if contour.nodes:
                first = contour.nodes[0]
                marks.append(Mark("text", ((first.x, first.y),), (56, 217, 137), text=str(len(contour.nodes))))
        return marks

docs.title: How bundles are installed and loaded
docs.text:
Point extensions in [tool.fontlab-install] at the folder that holds the kind subfolders, and declare the framework as a dependency:

[tool.fontlab-install]
id = "com.example.mytools"
name = "my-fontlab-tools"
extensions = "Extensions"
dependencies = ["fontlab-fontlabapp>=1.2.10", "fontlab-fly>=1.3.0"]

bootstrap links each bundle that holds a plugin.json to <data>/Extensions/<kind>/<Name>.fontlab<Kind>. At launch, fontlabapp.plugins discovers the bundles, imports their entry modules and registers them with FontLab's interface. A bundle with an invalid manifest or a failing import is logged and skipped; the other plugins still load.

Plugin code is trusted Python that runs in FontLab with full access. Restart FontLab to load a changed bundle.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
Run uvx fontlab-python-instamix, fontlab-instamix after installing, or python -m fontlab_instamix. Every command takes --data-dir.

Command Does env print Python, platform and FontLab folders as JSON ext install PATH… [--copy] [--run-hooks] install .fontlabext folders or .fontlabextz zips ext list list installed extensions: id, version and name, tab-separated ext uninstall ID… uninstall extensions by id pkg install SPEC… [--upgrade] install PyPI or git+ packages with uv pkg list list installed distributions pkg uninstall NAME… remove packages installed with pkg install wrap SOURCE --id ID [--name N] [--version V] [--out DIR] [--zip] wrap a script or folder into a .fontlabext bootstrap [PROJECT] [--copy] install a project checkout from its [tool.fontlab-install] uv fetch find uv or download it into <data>/python/uv venv create <data>/.venv for Python 3.11 stub FOLDER… [--force] write the install.vfpy stub into repository folders

Instamix runs uv as a separate program. It never runs sys.executable, which inside FontLab is FontLab itself.

docs.title: Remote commands
docs.text:
Install with uv tool install --upgrade 'fontlab-python-instamix[remote]', then run fontlab-instamix --remote env. Use a numbered Remopy release, 2.0.13 or later. Local build labels on those releases work too. Prereleases, development builds and unrecognized versions are refused. Use --remote with env, pkg, ext or venv. Put --bridge PATH before the command to select a specific Remopy bridge. Setup follows a bundled bridge to its FontLab app, including apps in the macOS user Applications folder. With an external bridge wrapper, setup uses the default installation or the user's Applications folder on macOS if the system installation is absent. Run extension hooks inside FontLab.

Remopy opens a setup .vfpy in FontLab before connecting to MCP. The script enables external MCP and turns on Hide warning dialogs. Both preferences persist. Installation starts after Remopy confirms the script ran, the tool catalogue responds and Instamix verifies the host data folder and shared access. After a setup timeout, inspect the reported files before trying again.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
import fontlab_instamix as im
im.install(path)           # a .fontlabext folder or .fontlabextz zip
im.uninstall(ext_id)       # returns the paths kept because they changed
im.installed()
im.install_project(path)   # a project checkout or its install.vfpy
im.data_dir()

docs.title: Manifest keys (manifest.fontlabextj)
docs.text: Key Meaning id reverse-DNS id, matching the folder name name display name version version string min_fontlab minimum FontLab version description short description python requires (PEP 508 list) and packages (folders) vars values for {var} in destinations install list of {"from": …, "to": …} entries

docs.title: Project keys ([tool.fontlab-install])
docs.text: Key Meaning id required reverse-DNS id name distribution name, used for the dist-info folder packages package folders for site-packages scripts folder of Scripts menu folders extensions folder of plugin bundles dependencies PEP 508 requirements, from PyPI or sibling checkouts init-script add the fontlabapp.plugins startup block to <data>/initScript.py; on by default only for com.fontlab.fontlabapp

docs.title: Plugin bundle (plugin.json)
docs.text: Key Meaning id unique across kinds; matches the class name name title; matches the class title kind reporter, filter, tool, palette or general version three-part version entry module:Class inside the bundle min_app_version minimum fontlabapp version
